title: Hot-shard rebalancing: move HOT without a route gap or two owners
requiredVisibleLabel: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Move a hot partition; detect routing gaps and simultaneous active owners.
sourceAcceptance: S065: Move tenants or partitions without missing writes or assigning two active owners. D-S065: Ownership changes preserve committed effects and routing; no two writers own the same moved partition, under actual live read/write load.
preconditions: A modern browser with local HTML, external CSS and JavaScript; no server or account.
Synthetic HOT starts on shard-old, epoch 7, with acknowledged effect H0.
Synthetic COLD stays on shard-cold with acknowledged effect C0.
Before, cutover and after each attempt one write and one read on both partitions.
The cutover target snapshot either includes acknowledged H1 or deliberately omits it.
actions: Choose hot routing, active-owner ordering, target copy and observation coverage.
Start to freeze exact inputs; observe the three fixed phases separately.
Inspect hot and cold routes, supplied owner epochs, acknowledged effects and operation outcomes.
Compare an optional learning prediction with the independent measured synthetic verdict.
Start another attempt with retained history, or explicitly reset all in-memory attempts.
assertions: Complete coordinated routing, exclusive ownership and a current target preserve all twelve operations.
A transient hot route gap remains failure after recovery.
A stale route reaches a fenced former owner and cannot pass.
Observed simultaneous hot owners fail even if all client operations succeed.
Missing acknowledged H1 fails despite correct routes and exclusive owners.
Missing observation coverage stays unknown; known failures dominate uncertainty.
COLD successes do not substitute for successful hot target exposure.
Exact input shapes, lifecycle, immutable snapshots and six-attempt history are guarded.

iac.decisionStage: After genuine behavioral RED and before behavior implementation
iac.reason: Resource-free local synthetic lesson; no cloud/IaC/scaffold/identity/deploy/spend.

testRuntime.purpose: Existing Node22 tooling only; not production Node24 certification.

limits: Fixed sequential synthetic fixtures, not a real partition, migration, routing or exclusive-ownership proof.
Supplied epochs and owner sets do not implement distributed fencing or concurrent execution.
The coordinated cutover is a model ordering, not a native atomicity guarantee.
No actual load, authentication, credentials, cloud operations, native Azure or production24 certification.
History retains at most six completed attempts in memory; explicit reset or reload clears it.
The abandoned browser lifecycle prototype is unqualified; no unattended-runner certification.
B-S065 and original D-S065 actual partition-rebalance acceptance remain separate and unfulfilled.
One frozen S unit; tests, evidence and refinement earn no additional units.
